Confirmed: Discussion [#13135](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/13135) reports a real limitation, still present on current HEAD (`ede84760b38a`). It has no replies yet.

Findings:

- `[dotfiles]` templates use the ordinary renderer, which does not register `secret()` ([files.rs](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/7301/mise/src/system/files.rs:1667)).
- `secret()` is registered only by the `[bootstrap.files]` renderer ([secrets.rs](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/7301/mise/src/system/secrets.rs:156)).
- `bootstrap dotfiles apply` has no `--prompt-secrets` option ([apply.rs](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/7301/mise/src/cli/dotfiles/apply.rs:22)).
- I reproduced both failures with a fresh current-HEAD build:
  - Supplying the secret through the environment still produces `Unknown function secret`.
  - Passing `--prompt-secrets` produces `unexpected argument '--prompt-secrets'`.
- This originated in PR [#11680](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/11680), which intentionally described secret inputs as a feature for “managed files.” The documentation likewise only demonstrates `[bootstrap.files]`; dotfile documentation lists the normal template context without `secret()`.

I’d classify this as a confirmed integration gap rather than user error. The reporter’s `[bootstrap.files]` workaround is currently the correct safe workaround.

A proper fix needs more than registering the function:

- Pass one request-scoped `SecretValues` resolver through dotfile apply/status/diff/unapply and aggregate bootstrap.
- Add `--prompt-secrets` where dotfile templates can be rendered.
- Preserve missing-secret preflight semantics.
- Explicitly redact `dotfiles diff`: it prints rendered patches directly to stdout ([files.rs](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/7301/mise/src/system/files.rs:3191)), while stdout helpers do not apply the logger’s redactor ([output.rs](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/7301/mise/src/output.rs:44)).
- Add end-to-end coverage proving secrets work and never appear in status, diff, dry-run, errors, or verbose output.
